newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Rabobank International buys 35 pct of Ukraine bank.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank International buys 35 pct of Ukraine bank.

text.p: The wholesale banking arm of Dutch Rabobank has bought a 35 percent stake in Kyivsky Mizhnarodny Bank (Kiev International Bank), wholesale unit chairman Arthur Arnold told a news conference on Thursday.
He said the Kiev bank's authorised capital would be raised to 10 million ecus from five million.

Rabobank bought its stake from Ukrainian Financial Group. Other investors in the bank are the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development with 35 percent, a Polish bank with 13.3 percent and Bank Ukraina with 16.7 percent.

The first deputy head of Ukraine's central bank, Volodymyr Bondar, told the same news conference that foreigners held six percent of the former Soviet republic's banking system, up one percentage point since the start of 1996 but still well below the central bank's 15 percent upper limit.
Ukraine is home to four purely foreign-owned banks -- Societe Generale and Credit Lyonnais of France, a Polish deposit bank and Russia's Inkombank-Ukraina, Bondar said.
Only 15 of Ukraine's 190 banks had any foreign investment, he said. Authorised capital in Ukrainian banks stood at $654.85 million on May 1, central bank data show.
Arnold said Kiev International Bank and Bank Ukraina would look at food and agriculture projects which needed long-term financing and at short-term trade financing needs.
Arnold's unit was set up last year as a Rabobank spin-off with some 3.5 billion guilders for mergers and acquisitions to 2000.
